additional_papers.authors: Andrea Dal Pozzolo, Olivier Caelen, Reid A. Johnson, Gianluca Bontempi
additional_papers.title: Calibrating Probability with Undersampling for Unbalanced Classification
additional_papers.venue: 2015 IEEE Symposium Series on Computational Intelligence (SSCI), Cape Town
additional_papers.key_finding: Undersampling the majority class shifts the posterior probabilities of a classifier; the paper derives a correction (Bayes-rule adjustment) so that probabilities learned on undersampled data are re-calibrated to the true class prior. This is the paper the Kaggle ULB dataset page cites as the origin of the 284,807-transaction / 492-fraud European dataset.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Cite as the dataset source. Motivates why probabilities from models trained with undersampling/SMOTE must be re-calibrated before a Low/Medium/High risk score is thresholded.

additional_papers.authors: Andrea Dal Pozzolo, Giacomo Boracchi, Olivier Caelen, Cesare Alippi, Gianluca Bontempi
additional_papers.title: Credit Card Fraud Detection: A Realistic Modeling and a Novel Learning Strategy
additional_papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
additional_papers.key_finding: Formalises the real-world FDS setting: concept drift, class imbalance and verification latency (only a small alerted subset is checked by investigators; most labels arrive days later). Proposes separating investigator feedback from delayed labels and evaluating with alert-based measures rather than plain accuracy.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Justifies the time-based train/val/test split and the use of precision-at-top-k / PR-AUC style metrics; frames delayed labels as future work for the online feature store.

additional_papers.authors: Andrea Dal Pozzolo, Giacomo Boracchi, Olivier Caelen, Cesare Alippi, Gianluca Bontempi
additional_papers.title: Credit card fraud detection and concept-drift adaptation with delayed supervised information
additional_papers.venue: 2015 International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IJCNN), Killarney
additional_papers.key_finding: Shows that investigator feedback and delayed labels must be handled separately; the winning strategy trains two classifiers (on feedbacks and on delayed labels) and aggregates them, substantially improving alert precision on real transactions.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Supports the two-model / aggregated-score design and explains how the system could be retrained under delayed labels in production.

additional_papers.authors: Andrea Dal Pozzolo, Olivier Caelen, Yann-Ael Le Borgne, Serge Waterschoot, Gianluca Bontempi
additional_papers.title: Learned lessons in credit card fraud detection from a practitioner perspective
additional_papers.key_finding: Practitioner-oriented comparison of imbalance handling, non-stationarity handling and evaluation metrics on real card data from a payment processor; highlights that metric choice and drift handling matter as much as the classifier.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Background for the imbalance-strategy comparison (none vs class-weight vs undersampling vs SMOTE) and for reporting several metrics.

additional_papers.authors: Alejandro Correa Bahnsen, Djamila Aouada, Aleksandar Stojanovic, Bjorn Ottersten
additional_papers.title: Feature engineering strategies for credit card fraud detection
additional_papers.key_finding: Transaction-aggregation features (per-card counts/amounts over time windows) and periodic time-of-day features modelled with the von Mises distribution improve detection; evaluation uses a cost-based (financial) measure rather than misclassification rate; code released.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Directly supports the per-card velocity counts, amount-vs-history ratios and night-time flags, and the cost-based thresholding.

additional_papers.authors: Christopher Whitrow, David J. Hand, Piotr Juszczak, David Weston, Niall M. Adams
additional_papers.title: Transaction aggregation as a strategy for credit card fraud detection
additional_papers.key_finding: Introduces transaction aggregation (summarising an account's recent activity into features) as a fraud-detection strategy and studies the effect of aggregation window length across classifiers on real bank data.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Foundational citation for the behavioural aggregation features and for choosing window lengths (time since last transaction, rolling counts).

additional_papers.authors: Fabrizio Carcillo, Yann-Ael Le Borgne, Olivier Caelen, Yacine Kessaci, Frederic Oble, Gianluca Bontempi
additional_papers.title: Combining unsupervised and supervised learning in credit card fraud detection
additional_papers.key_finding: A hybrid that feeds unsupervised outlier scores, computed at several granularity levels (global, per card, per cluster), into a supervised classifier improves detection accuracy on a real annotated card dataset.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: The closest published precedent for feeding Isolation Forest anomaly scores into the stacking meta-learner alongside XGBoost/RF outputs.

additional_papers.authors: Fabrizio Carcillo, Andrea Dal Pozzolo, Yann-Ael Le Borgne, Olivier Caelen, Yannis Mazzer, Gianluca Bontempi
additional_papers.title: SCARFF: a scalable framework for streaming credit card fraud detection with Spark
additional_papers.key_finding: Integrates Kafka, Spark and Cassandra with an ML approach handling imbalance, non-stationarity and feedback latency; shown scalable, efficient and accurate on a massive real transaction stream.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Architecture reference for the FastAPI real-time API + online feature store; shows what a production streaming version would add.

additional_papers.authors: Fabrizio Carcillo, Yann-Ael Le Borgne, Olivier Caelen, Gianluca Bontempi
additional_papers.title: Streaming active learning strategies for real-life credit card fraud detection: assessment and visualization
additional_papers.venue: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
additional_papers.key_finding: Journal extension of the DSAA 2017 paper (team paper 11): compares supervised, semi-supervised and unsupervised querying criteria for selecting which cardholders investigators should contact; High-Risk Querying is a strong baseline.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Supports the 'Step-up verification' tier as a human-in-the-loop querying mechanism whose labels can feed retraining.

additional_papers.authors: Bertrand Lebichot, Gian Marco Paldino, Wissam Siblini, Liyun He-Guelton, Frederic Oble, Gianluca Bontempi
additional_papers.title: Incremental learning strategies for credit cards fraud detection
additional_papers.venue: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
additional_papers.key_finding: Compares incremental (sliding-window / ensemble) learning strategies for adapting fraud detectors to concept drift on real Worldline data.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Future-work citation for periodic retraining of the stack as fraud patterns drift.

additional_papers.authors: Yann-Ael Le Borgne, Wissam Siblini, Bertrand Lebichot, Gianluca Bontempi
additional_papers.title: Reproducible Machine Learning for Credit Card Fraud Detection - Practical Handbook
additional_papers.venue: Universite Libre de Bruxelles (online book, Jupyter Book)
additional_papers.key_finding: Open, reproducible benchmark of essential fraud-detection techniques (simulated data, feature transformation, imbalance handling, ensembles, sequential/temporal validation, performance metrics) based on the ULB-Worldline collaboration; explicitly motivated by the lack of reproducibility in the field.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Template for the temporal validation protocol, delayed-label simulation and the choice of metrics; cite for the reproducibility argument.

additional_papers.authors: Johannes Jurgovsky, Michael Granitzer, Konstantin Ziegler, Sylvie Calabretto, Pierre-Edouard Portier, Liyun He-Guelton, Olivier Caelen
additional_papers.title: Sequence classification for credit-card fraud detection
additional_papers.key_finding: Frames fraud detection as sequence classification with LSTMs over per-card transaction histories; LSTM improves detection on face-to-face transactions versus a random forest, while feature aggregation strategies remain highly effective for both.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Supports using per-card history features with tree models now, and LSTM sequence models as future work.

additional_papers.authors: Nitesh V. Chawla, Kevin W. Bowyer, Lawrence O. Hall, W. Philip Kegelmeyer
additional_papers.title: SMOTE: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique
additional_papers.key_finding: Synthetic minority oversampling combined with majority undersampling improves classifier sensitivity to the minority class on imbalanced data.

additional_papers.authors: Scott M. Lundberg, Gabriel Erion, Hugh Chen, Alex DeGrave, Jordan M. Prutkin, Bala Nair, Ronit Katz, Jonathan Himmelfarb, Nisha Bansal, Su-In Lee
additional_papers.title: From local explanations to global understanding with explainable AI for trees
additional_papers.key_finding: TreeSHAP: polynomial-time exact Shapley values for tree ensembles, interaction values, and tools to build global understanding from many local explanations.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Reference for computing exact, fast SHAP values for XGBoost/RF at API time and for global feature-importance plots on the dashboard.

additional_papers.authors: Ismini Psychoula, Andreas Gutmann, Pradip Mainali, Sharon H. Lee, Paul Dunphy, Fabien Petitcolas
additional_papers.title: Explainable Machine Learning for Fraud Detection
additional_papers.key_finding: Explores explainability methods for real-time fraud detection, examining the choice of SHAP background datasets and run-time trade-offs on supervised and unsupervised models.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Supports the design decision to compute SHAP explanations inside the real-time API and to pick a background dataset carefully.

additional_papers.authors: Leo Grinsztajn, Edouard Oyallon, Gael Varoquaux
additional_papers.title: Why do tree-based models still outperform deep learning on typical tabular data?
additional_papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS 2022), Datasets and Benchmarks Track
additional_papers.key_finding: Benchmark of 45 tabular datasets: tree-based models (XGBoost, random forests) remain state of the art on medium-sized tabular data, even before accounting for their speed.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Justifies choosing tree ensembles over the CNN/LSTM approaches in team papers 1, 2, 9 and 10.

additional_papers.authors: Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Amitai Armon
additional_papers.title: Tabular data: Deep learning is not all you need
additional_papers.key_finding: XGBoost outperforms recent deep tabular models across datasets (including those the deep models were proposed on) and needs far less tuning; an ensemble of deep models and XGBoost does best.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Second, independent justification for the tree-based hybrid design and for ensembling.

additional_papers.authors: Takaya Saito, Marc Rehmsmeier
additional_papers.title: The Precision-Recall Plot Is More Informative than the ROC Plot When Evaluating Binary Classifiers on Imbalanced Datasets
additional_papers.key_finding: On strongly imbalanced data ROC curves can look deceptively good; precision-recall plots expose differences in false-positive behaviour that matter for the minority class.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Justifies reporting PR-AUC (average precision) as the primary metric and ROC-AUC only as secondary.

additional_papers.authors: Davide Chicco, Giuseppe Jurman
additional_papers.title: The advantages of the Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) over F1 score and accuracy in binary classification evaluation
additional_papers.key_finding: Accuracy and F1 can be over-optimistic on imbalanced data; MCC is high only when all four confusion-matrix cells are good.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Justifies adding MCC to the evaluation table and explains why '99.9% accuracy' claims in the literature are not informative.

additional_papers.authors: Miriam Seoane Santos, Jastin Pompeu Soares, Pedro Henriques Abreu, Helder Araujo, Joao Santos
additional_papers.title: Cross-Validation for Imbalanced Datasets: Avoiding Overoptimistic and Overfitting Approaches
additional_papers.key_finding: A frequent experimental flaw is applying oversampling to the entire dataset before cross-validation, producing biased models and overly optimistic estimates; oversampling must be done inside each training fold only.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Primary methodological citation for the 'SMOTE-before-split inflates results' demonstration.

additional_papers.authors: Shachar Kaufman, Saharon Rosset, Claudia Perlich, Ori Stitelman
additional_papers.title: Leakage in data mining: Formulation, detection, and avoidance
additional_papers.venue: ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data
additional_papers.key_finding: Formal definition of leakage (information about the target illegitimately available at training time), with detection and avoidance methodology; recommends 'learn-predict separation' respecting time.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Supports computing behavioural features only from past transactions (online feature store) and the time-ordered split.

additional_papers.authors: Ruben van den Goorbergh, Maarten van Smeden, Dirk Timmerman, Ben Van Calster
additional_papers.title: The harm of class imbalance corrections for risk prediction models: illustration and simulation using logistic regression
additional_papers.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association
additional_papers.key_finding: Random undersampling, oversampling and SMOTE produce strongly miscalibrated (over-estimated) risk probabilities without improving discrimination; imbalance correction is not needed when the output is a calibrated risk score with a chosen threshold.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Key argument for the calibrated risk score + cost-based threshold design over resampling, and for the calibration step after class weighting.

additional_papers.authors: Charles Elkan
additional_papers.title: The Foundations of Cost-Sensitive Learning
additional_papers.venue: Proceedings of the 17th International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI-01), Seattle
additional_papers.key_finding: Optimal decisions under a cost matrix reduce to thresholding a calibrated probability at p* = C_FP/(C_FP+C_FN); changing class balance in training mainly shifts the threshold and can be corrected analytically.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Theoretical basis for the cost-based Approve / Step-up / Block thresholds on the calibrated fraud probability.

additional_papers.authors: Alexandru Niculescu-Mizil, Rich Caruana
additional_papers.title: Predicting good probabilities with supervised learning
additional_papers.venue: Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML '05), Bonn
additional_papers.key_finding: Boosted trees push probabilities away from 0 and 1 (sigmoid distortion) while bagged trees/random forests are better calibrated; Platt scaling and isotonic regression fix the distortion.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Justifies calibrating the XGBoost/stack output (Platt or isotonic) before mapping to Low/Medium/High.

additional_papers.authors: Toon Vanderschueren, Tim Verdonck, Bart Baesens, Wouter Verbeke
additional_papers.title: Predict-then-optimize or predict-and-optimize? An empirical evaluation of cost-sensitive learning strategies
additional_papers.key_finding: Compares cost-sensitive training (predict-and-optimize) with cost-sensitive thresholding of a standard model (predict-then-optimize) across fraud and credit datasets; cost-sensitive decision rules on a well-trained model are a strong, simple option.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Supports the 'train normally, then set cost-based thresholds' approach adopted in the risk engine.

additional_papers.authors: Sebastiaan Hoppner, Bart Baesens, Wouter Verbeke, Tim Verdonck
additional_papers.title: Instance-dependent cost-sensitive learning for detecting transfer fraud
additional_papers.key_finding: Fraud detection is an instance-dependent cost-sensitive problem (the cost of a missed fraud equals the transaction amount); proposes cost-sensitive logistic regression / boosting optimising expected savings rather than AUC.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Justifies weighting the cost of false negatives by transaction amount when choosing thresholds and reporting 'savings' alongside F1.

additional_papers.authors: Joao Gama, Indre Zliobaite, Albert Bifet, Mykola Pechenizkiy, Abdelhamid Bouchachia
additional_papers.title: A survey on concept drift adaptation
additional_papers.key_finding: Taxonomy of concept-drift types and adaptive-learning strategies (detection, sliding windows, ensembles) and of evaluation methodology for evolving data.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Background for the drift discussion and for evaluating on a later time slice.

additional_papers.authors: Altyeb Altaher Taha, Sharaf Jameel Malebary
additional_papers.title: An Intelligent Approach to Credit Card Fraud Detection Using an Optimized Light Gradient Boosting Machine
additional_papers.key_finding: Bayesian-optimised LightGBM for card fraud detection evaluated on two public datasets (including the ULB dataset); reports strong accuracy/AUC versus other classifiers.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Comparator for gradient-boosting results on the ULB dataset; supports hyper-parameter optimisation of the boosting model.

additional_papers.authors: Fawaz Khaled Alarfaj, Iqra Malik, Hikmat Ullah Khan, Naif Almusallam, Muhammad Ramzan, Muzamil Ahmed
additional_papers.title: Credit Card Fraud Detection Using State-of-the-Art Machine Learning and Deep Learning Algorithms
additional_papers.key_finding: Comparative analysis of ML (ELM, DT, RF, SVM, LR, XGBoost) and CNN-based DL architectures on the European (ULB) benchmark dataset.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Widely cited ML-vs-DL comparator on the same ULB dataset.

additional_papers.authors: Ebenezer Esenogho, Ibomoiye Domor Mienye, Theo G. Swart, Kehinde Aruleba, George Obaido
additional_papers.title: A Neural Network Ensemble With Feature Engineering for Improved Credit Card Fraud Detection
additional_papers.key_finding: LSTM base learners in an AdaBoost ensemble with SMOTE-ENN resampling and feature engineering for imbalanced card fraud data.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Comparator for ensemble + feature-engineering designs; same first-author group as team paper 19.

additional_papers.authors: Yang Liu, Xiang Ao, Zidi Qin, Jianfeng Chi, Jinghua Feng, Hao Yang, Qing He
additional_papers.title: Pick and Choose: A GNN-based Imbalanced Learning Approach for Fraud Detection
additional_papers.key_finding: PC-GNN: label-balanced sampling of nodes/edges and neighbour choosing to counter class imbalance in graph-based fraud detection.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Future-work citation for graph-based extension using card-merchant-device relations.

additional_papers.authors: Prince Grover, Julia Xu, Justin Tittelfitz, Anqi Cheng, Zheng Li, Jakub Zablocki, Jianbo Liu, Hao Zhou
additional_papers.title: Fraud Dataset Benchmark and Applications
additional_papers.venue: arXiv preprint arXiv:2208.14417 (v1 Aug 2022, v3 Sep 2023), Amazon
additional_papers.key_finding: FDB compiles public fraud datasets (including card-not-present fraud) with standardised train/test splits and demonstrates feature engineering, supervised-model comparison, label-noise removal, class-imbalance treatment and semi-supervised learning.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Reference for standardised benchmarking and for the observation that fraud data have unique properties (imbalance, drift, adversarial).

additional_papers.authors: Khizar Hayat, Baptiste Magnier
additional_papers.title: Data Leakage and Deceptive Performance: A Critical Examination of Credit Card Fraud Detection Methodologies
additional_papers.key_finding: Identifies four flaws in card-fraud papers: leakage from preprocessing/oversampling before the split, vague reporting, no temporal validation, and recall optimisation at precision's expense; a minimal MLP with leakage reaches 99.9% recall, while a corrected pipeline gives modest but reliable metrics.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Direct peer-reviewed support for the SMOTE-before-split + random-split inflation experiment and the temporal split.

additional_papers.authors: Mohammad Shanaa, Sherief Abdallah
additional_papers.title: A Hybrid Anomaly Detection Framework Combining Supervised and Unsupervised Learning for Credit Card Fraud Detection
additional_papers.key_finding: Autoencoder reconstruction error (trained on normal transactions) fused with an XGBoost score via optimised thresholding on the ULB dataset (284,807 transactions, 492 frauds): recall 0.925, precision 0.957, F1 0.941, MCC 0.941; code and pipeline released.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Closest recent comparator to the XGBoost + anomaly-score hybrid on the same dataset; use its reported numbers as a benchmark.

additional_papers.authors: Saria Iqbal, Khalid Mahmood Awan, Shahid Kamal, Zahoor Ur Rehman
additional_papers.title: Interpretable Ensemble Learning Models for Credit Card Fraud Detection
additional_papers.key_finding: Combines Random Forest and XGBoost with SHAP and LIME on a real-world card-fraud dataset, arguing that systematic XAI is scarce in fraud work and is required for regulatory compliance and trust.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Supports SHAP-based reason codes for RF/XGBoost outputs.

additional_papers.authors: Elif Zulal Cavdar, Aysun Bozanta
additional_papers.title: AI-based credit card fraud detection: a machine learning approach with model explainability on real-world data
additional_papers.key_finding: Nine supervised/unsupervised models under four sampling schemes (imbalanced, undersampling, SMOTE, voting+undersampling) on a private real dataset and a public one; Random Forest best among ML models, TabTransformer among DL; tuned XGBoost had a statistically higher F1 but RF was more robust without tuning; explained with feature importance, SHAP, LIME and DeepLIFT.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Supports keeping both RF and XGBoost in the stack and comparing sampling strategies; recent XAI precedent on real bank data.

additional_papers.authors: Francis Thiong'o, Lawrence Nderu, Ronald Waweru Mwangi, Isaac Nyabisa Oteyo
additional_papers.title: A drift adaptive framework for detecting and tracking evolving anomalies in financial transaction streams
additional_papers.key_finding: HADA+ hybrid anomaly-detection architecture with drift-responsive prioritisation and lifecycle tracking; on the (ULB) Credit Card Fraud dataset reports ROC-AUC 0.915 and PR-AUC 0.069 for the unsupervised setting, illustrating how much lower PR-AUC is than ROC-AUC on this data.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Recent evidence for concept-drift handling and for the ROC-vs-PR gap on the ULB dataset; supports using PR-AUC.

additional_papers.authors: Nguyen Duy Anh Luong, Shengkun Xie
additional_papers.title: Explainable ensemble machine learning for financial transaction fraud detection: Insights from XGBoost and deep neural networks
additional_papers.venue: The Journal of Finance and Data Science
additional_papers.key_finding: XGBoost + DNN ensemble using transactional, temporal and identity-linked features; evaluates focal loss, class weighting and threshold optimisation for imbalance; SHAP for interpretability on a real transaction dataset.
additional_papers.apply_to_our_system: Supports class-weighting + threshold optimisation over resampling, and SHAP in a regulated setting.

industry_context.claim: Global payment-card fraud losses (issuers, merchants, acquirers, ATM processors) in 2024
industry_context.figure: USD 33.41 billion in 2024 (down 1.2% year on year) on USD 51.920 trillion of card volume; 6.43 cents per USD 100 (down from 6.58 cents in 2023); the US accounted for 26.31% of card volume but 41.87% of fraud losses; projected USD 41.06 billion by 2030 and USD 48.50 billion by 2034 (cumulative USD 407.60 billion over the next 10 years)
industry_context.source: The Nilson Report, press release 'Global Card Fraud Losses at $33 Billion' (GlobeNewswire)

industry_context.claim: Long-run growth of global card fraud losses (historical trend)
industry_context.figure: USD 9.84 billion (2011) to USD 27.85 billion (2018), projected to exceed USD 40 billion by 2027 (2019 Nilson Report as quoted in the ULB handbook foreword); the same foreword notes the fraud-loss percentage began to decline in 2016 alongside adoption of ML-based detection
industry_context.source: Le Borgne et al., Reproducible Machine Learning for Credit Card Fraud Detection - Practical Handbook, Foreword (citing Nilson Report 2019)

industry_context.claim: Payment fraud in the European Economic Area, 2024
industry_context.figure: Total reported payment fraud EUR 4.2 billion in 2024 (EUR 3.5 billion in 2023, EUR 3.4 billion in 2022); card-payment fraud losses on EU/EEA-issued cards EUR 1.329 billion in 2024 (+29% y/y); overall fraud rate about 0.002% of transaction value; card fraud was 17 times higher when the payee was outside the EEA where strong customer authentication is not required
industry_context.source: EBA-ECB joint 2025 Report on Payment Fraud, ECB press release

industry_context.claim: Card-not-present (CNP) fraud share of total card fraud value (Europe)
industry_context.figure: In 2019, 80% of the value of card fraud on SEPA-issued cards came from CNP transactions (internet, mail, phone) - EUR 1.50 billion of EUR 1.87 billion total; point-of-sale fraud 15% and ATM fraud 5%
industry_context.source: European Central Bank, Seventh report on card fraud

industry_context.claim: UK unauthorised fraud and remote-purchase (CNP) fraud, 2024
industry_context.figure: 3.13 million unauthorised fraud cases (+14%) and GBP 722 million losses (+2%) in 2024; remote purchase fraud cases +22% to nearly 2.6 million and losses +11% to just under GBP 400 million, driven partly by social engineering of one-time passcodes; card ID theft losses fell 26% to GBP 58.7 million; GBP 1.45 billion of unauthorised fraud was prevented (67p per GBP 1 attempted); customers refunded in >98% of unauthorised cases
industry_context.source: UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report 2025 press release

industry_context.claim: India: bank frauds reported to RBI (frauds of Rs 1 lakh and above), latest three years
industry_context.figure: 2025-26: 10,114 cases / Rs 48,021 crore; 2024-25: 23,722 cases / Rs 32,803 crore; 2023-24: 35,800 cases / Rs 11,013 crore (Table VI.2). Card/Internet/Digital-payments category: 28,836 cases (80.4% of all cases) / Rs 1,452 crore in 2023-24; 13,332 cases (56.2%) / Rs 517 crore in 2024-25; 293 cases (2.9%) / Rs 29 crore in 2025-26 (Table VI.3). RBI notes card/internet frauds were the most numerous category in 2023-24 and 2024-25, and that 2025-26 data include 314 re-classified older cases worth Rs 30,199 crore
industry_context.source: Reserve Bank of India, Annual Report 2025-26, Chapter VI (Regulation, Supervision and Financial Stability), Tables VI.2 and VI.3

industry_context.claim: India: bank fraud figures as first published in the previous RBI Annual Report (before revisions)
industry_context.figure: 2024-25: 23,953 cases / Rs 36,014 crore (amount roughly three times 2023-24's Rs 12,230 crore; case count down from 36,060) - secondary reporting of RBI Annual Report 2024-25; the 2025-26 report later shows revised 2024-25 figures of 23,722 cases / Rs 32,803 crore
industry_context.source: RBI Annual Report 2024-25 as reported by Deccan Herald and SBI Ecowrap (secondary sources; the RBI PDF is behind a bot-check)

industry_context.claim: India: customer liability rules for unauthorised electronic banking transactions
industry_context.figure: RBI circular RBI/2017-18/15, DBR.No.Leg.BC.78/09.07.005/2017-18 'Customer Protection - Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions': zero customer liability for bank negligence or third-party breach reported within 3 working days; limited liability (max Rs 10,000 for credit cards with limit up to Rs 5 lakh, Rs 25,000 above) if reported within 4-7 working days; banks must shadow-credit the amount within 10 working days and resolve within 90 days; burden of proof lies on the bank; banks must have a 'robust and dynamic fraud detection and prevention mechanism' and mandatory SMS alerts; distinguishes CNP/remote from card-present transactions

industry_context.claim: India: regulatory requirements for digital payment security and fraud risk management
industry_context.figure: RBI Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls (RBI/2020-21/74, DoS.CO.CSITE.SEC.No.1852/31.01.015/2020-21), effective six months after issue: para 36-37 require documented rules and parameterised alerts on transaction velocity, high-risk merchant category codes, counterfeit-card/CVV patterns, new-account activity, time zones, geo-locations, IP origin and behavioural biometrics; para 34 allows adaptive (risk-based) authentication; para 41 requires near-real-time reconciliation; para 72 requires 24x7 monitoring of card transactions with card/BIN-level limits; para 39 requires staff able to 'differentiate false positives from the rest'
industry_context.source: Reserve Bank of India, Master Direction on Digital Payment Security Controls

industry_context.claim: ULB/Worldline European credit-card dataset (Kaggle mlg-ulb/creditcardfraud) size and imbalance
industry_context.figure: 284,807 transactions with 492 frauds (about 0.172%); PCA-anonymised features V1-V28 plus Time and Amount; originates from the ULB Machine Learning Group - Worldline collaboration (Dal Pozzolo et al., 2015)
industry_context.source: Figures confirmed in peer-reviewed abstracts using the dataset (Shanaa & Abdallah 2025, F1000Research 14:664; Jayasingh & Sri 2023, ESCI); Kaggle page itself could not be fetched automatically

industry_context.figure: Generated with the open-source 'Sparkov Data Generation' synthetic credit-card transaction generator (Brandon Harris, namebrandon/Sparkov_Data_Generation, originally based on code by Josh Plotkin); v0.3 of the generator introduced fraudulent transactions/profiles and Gamma-distributed amounts; customer profiles, merchant names and spending-category windows are simulated
industry_context.source: GitHub repository README (Kaggle page could not be fetched automatically; row counts of fraudTrain/fraudTest not verified here)
